latest_evidence.semantic_conclusion: Finite tombstone retention is safe only when the entire duplicate/retry universe for the same logical effect is closed by a standards/protocol bound and the effect identity is atomically bound to that bounded identity. CoAP supplies a finite EXCHANGE_LIFETIME for exact Message ID reuse (247 seconds with default parameters), but that does not bound higher-layer retries that create a new logical request. HTTP defines retry semantics and minimum Retry-After delays but no general maximum logical-operation retry horizon, so HTTP does not justify a universal finite tombstone TTL. Without trustworthy elapsed time, require an authoritative closed epoch that excludes old identities; otherwise retain identity non-reuse indefinitely. Hidden side effects require atomic coupling or independent idempotence.
